artworks.title: Telemachus Departing from Nestor
artworks.description: Henry Howard's painting, long reproduced as the standard illustration of Odyssey 3, shows young Telemachus taking leave of Nestor at sandy Pylos — the garrulous king who first shelters Odysseus's son and fills him with tales of Troy. Bearded wisdom and youthful resolve face each other under an open sky, the visual shorthand for Nestor as counsellor of the next generation. The image still headlines many modern retellings of the Telemachy.

artworks.title: Achilles Presented to Nestor
artworks.description: Court's Neoclassical canvas presents the boy Achilles before Nestor — the Pylian king cast as the aged arbiter of heroic education, the same voice Homer gives him in the Iliad as the eldest counsellor at Troy. Academic clarity and theatrical gesture turn the meeting into a lesson in respect for experience. The painting belongs to the nineteenth-century French taste for Homeric pedagogy, with Nestor as the living archive of the previous generation's wars.

artworks.title: Achilles Gives Nestor the Prize of Wisdom
artworks.description: In this companion scene by Court, Achilles awards Nestor a prize for wisdom — a pictorial gloss on the Iliad's funeral games and on Nestor's standing as the Achaeans' remembered counsellor. The king of Pylos receives the tribute of youth before assembled heroes, his age turned into public honour rather than frailty. French academic painting here cements the epithet that English still borrows: a nestor as a wise old adviser.

artworks.title: Telemachus and Nestor Embracing
artworks.description: This 1732 proof engraving in the Rijksmuseum (RP-P-OB-52.057), from a series illustrating Fénelon's Avonturen van Telemachus, shows Telemachus and Nestor locked in an embrace amid onlookers, horse and armour at the edge of the plate. The print carries the Homeric hospitality of Odyssey 3 into the eighteenth-century bestseller that made Telemachus a European schoolbook hero. Nestor appears as the warm, paternal king of Pylos — counsel given as welcome.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky's miniseries keeps Nestor as the garrulous king of Pylos — Telemachus' first harbour of counsel on the search for Odysseus.

films.title: Troy
films.description: John Shrapnel's Nestor is Agamemnon's grey counsellor — the Pylian king who steers the Greek council toward Achilles and the ships.

films.title: Helen of Troy
films.description: Wise's epic keeps Guido Notari's Nestor among the Greek kings — the eldest voice at the council that launches the thousand ships.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Rossi's Italian-Yugoslav miniseries sends Telemachus to Jaspar von Oertzen's Nestor at Pylos — the Homeric harbour of counsel before Sparta.

popCulture.title: Troilus and Cressida
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: Shakespeare's Greek camp keeps Nestor as the 'wise and talkative' prince — Homer's garrulous counsellor translated into bitter comedy.

popCulture.title: Les Aventures de Télémaque
popCulture.creator: François Fénelon
popCulture.description: Fénelon's pedagogical romance still opens Telemachus' voyage at Nestor's Pylos — the Homeric host rewritten as a mirror for princes.
